correctness.rationale: The unitary projection proof establishes rank >= |R||C|/|G| and an exact iff via commutation, full row translation stabilizer and Fourier inversion. For |R|=|C|=6 in Z12, subgroup divisibility and pair classification prove exactly 76 minimum-rank pairs. Integer orbit representatives and two independent modular Gaussian rank implementations give rank histogram (76,5376,150564,697760); the product of two verified good primes exceeds the Hadamard upper bound for absolute norms of all minors up to size six, so modular vanishing lifts rigorously to complex vanishing. Both standalone verifiers ran and their outputs and certificate are included. Independent validation not claimed.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The full-spark result classifies existence of a singular maximal minor, not six-row/six-column ranks. The full published fifth-order incidence concerns size five, not six. Delvaux–Van Barel gives related constructions and extremal support bounds, but no inspected explicit theorem yields the six-by-six histogram or all 76 equality cases. A hidden implicit consequence remains possible.

value.rationale: Order twelve at half sampling is a natural composite harmonic interpolation benchmark. The exact number of configurations losing one, two, or three directions is not obtainable from singular-minor counts, and precisely 76 sharp losses admit a structural description. The finite abelian projection-commutation criterion explains the extremal mechanism beyond one matrix size and makes the exact fact useful for rank-deficient sampling designs. The result does not claim general all-rank profiles or stability bounds.
